Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

adopt verb

take up a custom, a word, a way of doing things

also take up, take over (a custom), borrow (a word, a custom), adopt a custom, adopt a plan, embrace (an idea)

classical

Liv. 1.20.6: patriōs rītūs peregrīnōsque adscīscendō
Cic. Verr. 2.5.187: ā Graecīs adscīta et accepta
Hor. Ep. 2.2.119, of new words (Lewis & Short)

ascīscō (adscīscō), ascīscere, ascīvī, ascītum

verb, third conjugation, transitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

adopt, take up (rites, laws, customs, words); take in (a person as ally or citizen)

To take something over from others and make it one’s own, with thought or effort behind it (Lewis & Short): foreign rites, a law passed elsewhere, new words. Of persons, to receive someone as citizen, ally or son. The editions spell it both asc- and adsc-; quotations keep their edition’s spelling.

Other words

  • cōnsilium capere — adopt a plan, decide on a course

    phrase: cōnsilium capere + gen. of the gerund(ive), or ut + subjunctive · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.2: legiōnis opprimendae cōnsilium capere (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 7.10: subitō cōnsilium cēpī, ut exīrem (Lewis & Short)

  • adoptō, adoptāre, adoptāvī, adoptātum — choose, take for oneself (a patron, a helper)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 54: quem sibi illa dēfēnsōrem suī jūris adoptāvit (Lewis & Short, as Div. in Caecin. 16); Traupman 269 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Its first sense, “take to oneself by choice”, used of persons; for an idea or a custom, ascīscere is the classical word. The common sense is to adopt a child (see adopt, a child).

Examples

  • nē quid dīvīnī jūris neglegendō patriōs rītūs peregrīnōsque adscīscendō turbārētur

    so that no part of divine law should be thrown into confusion by neglecting the native rites and adopting foreign onesLiv. 1.20.6

  • quārum sacra populus Rōmānus ā Graecīs adscīta et accepta tantā religiōne et pūblicē et prīvātim tuētur

    whose rites the Roman people took over from the Greeks and keep with such devotion, in public and in privateCic. Verr. 2.5.187

See also adopt, practice, introduce, foreign.
